Senses.Explanation: The fixed four-character string names the stock particles of bookish Classical Chinese and is used to mock literary learning when it substitutes for realization. A verse, Yang Jie's death poem, Zhantang's verse, Dahui's instruction, Tianyin Yuanxiu, and Liangting Jingting supply six distinct deployments of the bookish-particle string.

Occurrences.Kwic: 天高地厚問端繇，棒喝交馳卒未休，換骨洗腸猶不是，誰知屋裏販揚州？

Senses.Explanation: This stock appraisal pictures redundant commerce: trying to sell all of Yangzhou while already inside one’s own house. Chan records apply the scene in encounters and verses. Its deployments retain the impossible redundancy of selling a whole place from inside one’s own house; local cases decide whom the appraisal addresses. The stored witnesses span 5 independent works and preserve the exact headword in the quoted Chinese. The gloss reports the shared deployment and leaves each surrounding case to its own recorded exchange.

Senses.Explanation: Bring out the treasures of one's own house follows the opening of one's own storehouse and names the use of resources described as already belonging there. Dahui applies the phrase to Shuilao after his exchange with Mazu; Huolian uses it in a postface; Luo’an Huiwen tells the assembly to distribute that household treasure at the crossroads; Jixiang Faxuan joins it to cutting off the sages’ tongues.

Senses.Explanation: Carrying water and moving firewood are ordinary tasks in the daily work of a household or monastery. Yibian names them as timely work; Tianyin asks who is carrying water and moving firewood all day; Ruibai tells listeners to farm, hoe, carry water, and move wood rather than seek elsewhere. Other records use the pair in biography and hall speech. The actions stay concrete even when a question turns on their actor.
